subject: Cross-region demo scheduling — spring changeover week
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@finera.com>, Finera Scheduling <scheduling@finera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-region demo scheduling — spring changeover week

Hi Elena / Finera scheduling team,

Thanks again for the interest — excited to get a walkthrough scheduled. I wanted to flag that the week of Mar 29–Apr 4 includes the US spring clock change but not the EU change, so there are some odd offsets between US / UK and your APAC folks.

Quick ask: can you share 2–3 blocks (30–45m) that work from your side, and indicate whether the preferred attendees are West-coast/EMEA/APAC-focused? I want to propose slots that avoid the mismatched hour window for the primary stakeholders.

We can run the demo from our side either:
- US-friendly window: 08:00–11:00 PT (16:00–19:00 CET) — good for Americas + early EMEA
- EMEA-friendly window: 13:00–16:00 PT (21:00–00:00 CET) — awkward for APAC
- APAC-friendly window: 22:00–01:00 PT (06:00–09:00 AEST) — late for US leadership

If you list preferred regions per attendee I can give a recommended slot and include a fallback canary time in case the US/UK clock jump causes calendar ambiguity. I've attached a short fallback plan and an .ics with my availability.

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@finera.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Cross-region demo scheduling — spring changeover week

Thanks Priyom — timing constraints below.

Attendees:
- Elena Ruiz (EU, Madrid) — prefers 15:00–17:00 CET
- Tom Wu (UK/EMEA lead) — flexible mornings GMT
- Payments team (APAC liaison) — can do 08:00–10:00 AEST but would prefer that to be early EU / late US only if unavoidable

We'd like a 45-minute demo plus 15 for Q&A.

Proposed candidate slots (in CET):
- Tue Mar 30, 16:00–17:00 CET
- Wed Mar 31, 15:30–16:15 CET (tight)

Note: Tom will be traveling Mar 29–30; if we pick Mar 30, please confirm timezone mapping so the calendar invite lands correctly for him. Our scheduling system (scheduling@finera.com) sometimes creates separate invites for GMT vs CET attendees which complicates things during the spring change week.

—Elena
Director of Product — Finera
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@finera.com>, Tom Wu <tom.wu@orbitalbank.co.uk>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-region demo scheduling — spring changeover week

Thanks Elena — that helps. I've mapped the candidate CET slots to PT/GMT/AEST below and included a recommended fallback: a secondary UTC-anchored invite to avoid local calendar conversions during the changeover.

Candidate slot A: Tue Mar 30, 16:00–16:45 CET
- CET: 16:00–16:45
- GMT: 15:00–15:45
- PT: 08:00–08:45
- AEST: 02:00–02:45 (not ideal for APAC)

Candidate slot B: Wed Mar 31, 15:30–16:15 CET
- CET: 15:30–16:15
- GMT: 14:30–15:15
- PT: 07:30–08:15
- AEST: 01:30–02:15

Fallback (UTC anchored): Tue Mar 30, 15:00–15:45 UTC — if a system splits invites by zone this single UTC invite should attach and display consistently.

Recommendation: pick Candidate A if Tom can accept the travel day; otherwise pick the UTC-anchored fallback and ask the scheduling system to use the event's primary timezone = UTC. We will send a mirrored calendar invite from our side with explicit timezone tags to reduce confusion.

Attaching a two-page PDF with the fallback plan and a small troubleshooting checklist (attachment). I'll wait for confirmation and will submit a calendar invite with all three slots as options (accept one, decline others).

Priyom
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
